According to a well-known leaker with a proven track record, next year is expected to witness the largest iPhone screen ever.

Supply chain sources indicate that Apple is testing a brand-new display, which may be used in an iPhone model whose name remains a mystery so far…

The Mystery of Next Year's Flagship iPhone Naming

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and there have long been rumours that Apple is preparing a special product to celebrate this milestone. The year is expected to be the closest Apple has come to realising its long-held vision of an "all-glass" iPhone.

There are rumours that Apple may follow the approach of the iPhone X and release a standalone 20th anniversary edition iPhone. However, more recent reports suggest that this revolutionary new design will debut as next year's Pro models, namely the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

A third possibility is that Apple, to celebrate the anniversary, will skip the iPhone 18 and go straight to the iPhone 20.

The Largest iPhone Screen Ever

Leaker "Digital Chat Station" (DCS) said that supply chain information indicates Apple is testing the largest iPhone screen to date. However, the size increase is only marginally larger than the current iPhone 17 Pro Max's 6.9-inch display.

In other words, they believe Apple will use "equipped with a 7-inch screen" as the key marketing point for this device.

DCS does not have information on the purpose of this new display—assuming Apple ultimately puts it into production—but speculates it may be used for next year's iPhone Pro Max, though the final name of the model remains unknown.

9to5Mac's Perspective

Apple tests countless products, most of which never see the light of day, so even if this display does exist in prototype form within the company's supply chain, it does not necessarily mean it will end up being used in an iPhone.

That said, if Apple's goal is to achieve an "all-glass" appearance, being able to boast the "largest screen ever" would indeed be a logical element in that pursuit.
